title: Computer Vision, Perception, and Robotic Manipulation Foundations

sources.notes: MIT OCW machine vision course identity for symbolic descriptions from images, image formation, image analysis, binary image processing, filtering, robotics applications, and intelligent machine-environment interaction.
OCW lecture-note index for machine vision topics; PDF lecture notes, diagrams, images, examples, and linked assets remain child-resource boundaries.
OCW project page for graduate final-project instructions and suggested topics; student submissions, code, data, and linked resources remain boundary-checked.

MIT OCW advanced computer vision course identity for image formation, representation theory, multi-view geometry, differentiable rendering, neural scene representations, correspondence, optical flow, point tracking, image/video generation, diffusion guidance, contrastive/masking representation learning, and vision for embodied agents.
External course site links recordings, slides, problem sets, projects, and course platforms; do not treat as OCW-cleared corpus text until terms and child artifacts are reviewed.

MIT OCW robotic manipulation course identity for autonomous manipulation in unstructured environments, perception using deep learning and 3D geometry, planning, kinematics, trajectory generation, collision-free motion planning, task-and-motion planning, uncertainty, dynamics, and control.
External robotic manipulation textbook identity; textbook pages, notebooks, code, figures, videos, simulation assets, and linked resources require dedicated reuse review.

Richard Szeliski Computer Vision: Algorithms and Applications identity; the site permits personal PDF download but says not to repost it, so book text, PDF, figures, slides, course links, and derived assets remain boundary-checked.

Stanford CS231n identity for deep learning architectures and end-to-end visual recognition tasks including image classification, localization, detection, training, fine-tuning, assignments, and projects; pages, assignments, code, datasets, demos, videos, and linked assets remain boundary-checked.
OpenCV documentation identity for versioned Doxygen HTML and release documentation; generated docs, archives, source code, samples, images, binaries, and package artifacts remain boundary-checked.

ROS 2 documentation identity for robot application libraries and tools, drivers, algorithms, developer tools, tutorials, concepts, package documentation, and citations; docs, packages, examples, generated docs, images, diagrams, and releases remain boundary-checked.

MoveIt identity for ROS motion planning, manipulation, kinematics, control, 3D perception, collision checking, setup, task construction, and grasp generation; docs, code, screenshots, demos, meshes, robot configs, and releases remain boundary-checked.

Drake identity for C++/Python robot dynamics, control systems, optimization-based design and analysis, simulation, planning, control, examples, tutorials, and benchmarks; docs, notebooks, source, binaries, examples, images, and releases remain boundary-checked.
